name: Polo the Penguin and Trees
description: Little penguin Polo has got a tree — a non-directed connected acyclic graph, containing n nodes and n - 1 edges. We will consider the tree nodes numbered by integers from 1 to n . Today Polo wonders, how to find the number of pairs of paths that don't have common nodes. More formally, he should find the number of groups of four integers a , b , c and d such that: 1 ≤ a < b ≤ n ; 1 ≤ c < d ≤ n ; there's no such node that lies on both the shortest path from node a to node b and from node c to node d . The shortest path betweem two nodes is the path that is shortest in the number of edges. Help Polo solve this problem.
input_specification: The first line contains integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 80000) — the number of tree nodes. Each of the following n - 1 lines contains a pair of integers u i and v i (1 ≤ u i , v i ≤ n ; u i ≠ v i ) — the i -th edge of the tree. It is guaranteed that the given graph is a tree.
output_specification: In a single line print a single integer — the answer to the problem. Please do not use the %lld specificator to read or write 64-bit numbers in С++. It is recommended to use the cin, cout streams or the %I64d specificator.
approach_summary: Precompute 2^k ancestor jumps up[u][k] and node depths in O(N log N). Compute LCA and path aggregates in O(log N) per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 288D — Polo the Penguin and Trees  [146. Binary Lifting and LCA]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary lifting for lowest common ancestor and tree jumps.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Any ancestor jump of distance $K$ can be decomposed into powers of two $K = \sum 2^j$. Precomputing `up[u][k]` (the $2^k$-th ancestor of $u$) via `up[u][k] = up[up[u][k-1]][k-1]` allows any path or LCA to be answered in $O(\log N)$.
